_comment: CANONICAL forbidden-phrase blocklist. CROSS-REPO-TUTORIAL-PRODUCER-GATE-W1.
This file is the ONE source. crypto-quant-signal-mcp reads it directly;
algovault-skills carries a VENDORED copy plus a committed .sha256 of THIS file,
and a parity assertion in each repo. The row below is the only canonical hash
reference point — the vendored copy never records a second hash of its own,
because a second recorded hash is a second thing that can drift.
WHY A PATTERN, NOT A LITERAL LIST: 'HOLDs are free', 'free HOLD' and 'HOLD
verdicts are never charged' are one class. A literal list lets the next
paraphrase through, which is exactly the defect this gate exists to make
impossible.
WHY NO BRAND-FACTS PROSE: brand-facts.md is private (vault). Only the
machine-checkable pattern and a citation travel into this public repo — same
discipline as ops/claudemd-claims.lock.json, which carries identifiers only.
RETIRED 2026-08-09 — `per-day-quota` (pattern \b\d+\s*(free\s*)?calls?\s*/?\s*(per\s*)?day\b,
correction '100 calls/month'). Its reason was 'Free tier is a monthly cap. Per-day
phrasing overstates it.' Architect ruling R-B introduced a REAL per-UTC-day cap
(free 100/day, Starter 1,000/day, Pro 10,000/day), so the premise is now false and
'100 calls/day' is an accurate statement the gate was blocking. A guard whose
premise a later wave invalidates must be RETIRED WITH ITS FIXTURES, not exempted
per-path — the exemption for the runbook that quoted the ban went with it, and the
runbook's authoring rule was rewritten rather than left describing a dead ban.
SCOPE: one phrase class at a time. Widening is OPS-BRAND-BLOCKLIST-WIDEN-W{NEXT}.

exempt_paths.reason: The runbook that DOCUMENTS this ban has to quote the banned phrase to be useful ('Never write that HOLD is free'). Comment-stripping cannot help — it is markdown prose, not a comment. CLAUDE.md gate-writing bug (a): a gate that demands the deletion of the line explaining the defect is a gate that gets disabled. Exemption is declared HERE on the row, never in prose, so a future wave enforcing the contract cannot silently 'fix' it. This row REPLACES the identical one that covered the retired `per-day-quota` class — same file, same reason, new phrase.

exempt_consumers.what: the free-HOLD purge registry in this repo
exempt_consumers.example: tests/unit/no-free-hold-promise.test.ts names `free_hold` and `holdFree` as behaviour identifiers
exempt_consumers.why: Behaviour identifiers, code comments and historical correction records are EXEMPT per the 2026-08-05 scope ruling; this blocklist scans reader-facing SURFACES (landing/**, docs/**, README) and never src/ or tests/, so the two guards do not overlap. The pattern is also directional — it requires HOLD adjacent to a free/never-charged claim, so 'Free tier: 200 calls/month' and 'Every verdict counts, HOLD included' are both inert.

phrases.correction: quota is counted per call, regardless of verdict
phrases.reason: Flat billing (R-A): every successful verdict is one metered call on BOTH rails. 'HOLD is free' was true until 2026-08-09 and is now a pricing misstatement — the most expensive kind, because ~99% of verdicts ARE holds.
